description: Create a one-off or recurring event on an inbox's calendar, with this inbox as organizer. start and end are local wall-clock times in timezone (the calendar's default, UTC unless changed, when omitted); the result also gives them as UTC instants. With sendInvites the inbox emails every attendee an invitation right away, which cannot be recalled; without it attendees are only listed. Retrying with the same clientId returns the event already created instead of a second one. Calendar works for every organization in US production; EU production returns 403 "Calendar isn't available in this region yet".

allDay.description: true for an all-day event, with start and end as dates

attendees.description: People to invite, at most 100; they are emailed only with sendInvites

comment.description: Note the attendee sent with their response; when replacing the list, keep the one get_event returned

email.description: Attendee's email address, unique within the event

name.description: Name shown for the attendee in the invitation

respondedAt.description: When the attendee last responded; when replacing the list, keep the one get_event returned

role.description: Whether their presence is required (the default) or optional

status.description: Their response so far, needs_action when omitted; when replacing the list, keep each status get_event returned

clientId.description: Your idempotency key: creating again with the same clientId and fields returns the event already created

description.description: Details attendees see in the invitation

end.description: Local end in the same format as start: after start for a timed event; for an all-day event, the last day (inclusive)

inboxId.description: Inbox ID: the inbox's email address, from list_inboxes

location.description: A place or a meeting link

metadata.description: Your own JSON object, returned when the event is read; never sent to attendees

exdates.description: Dates to skip, each the original start of a date: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss for a timed event, YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day one

rdates.description: Extra dates the rule does not produce: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss for a timed event, YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day one, or for a timed event a period

duration.description: ISO 8601 length of the extra date, e.g. PT30M; give end or duration

end.description: Local end of the extra date; give end or duration

start.description: Local start of the extra date, YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss

rule.description: RFC 5545 RRULE evaluated in the event's timezone from its start, e.g. FREQ=WEEKLY;BYDAY=MO,WE,FR or FREQ=MONTHLY;BYDAY=-1FR;COUNT=12

sendInvites.description: Email every attendee the invitation (one send per attendee against send limits). Applies to this request only, so pass it again on each change attendees should hear about. Only for events this inbox organizes

start.description: Local start in timezone, without an offset: YYYY-MM-DDTHH:mm:ss for a timed event, YYYY-MM-DD for an all-day one; for a recurring event, its first date

status.description: confirmed (the default), or tentative for a hold that is not settled

timezone.description: Time zone of start and end; the calendar's default (see get_calendar) when omitted. IANA time zone, e.g. America/New_York, Europe/London or UTC. Any case and aliases such as US/Eastern are accepted and stored under the canonical name, which can differ from the spelling sent; abbreviations such as PST and UTC offsets are refused
